title: Primary in-distribution leakage and semantic utility

conventions.fold_combination: within-seed: mean of fold AUCs; retrieval hits pooled over folds
conventions.difference: paired by seed, then mean and sample SD of the per-seed differences
conventions.ood_interval: saved 95% paired query bootstrap, 10,000 draws, seed 0

caption: Primary in-distribution leakage and semantic utility. Cells are the mean $\pm$ sample SD ($\mathrm{ddof}{=}1$) across fitting seeds. Each seed's score is computed within that seed; SemEval's five outer folds are combined within each seed (fold AUCs averaged, held-out retrieval hits pooled), and nothing is pooled across seeds. Seeds: SemEval 5 seeds (0--4); SwiLTra 5 seeds (0--4); Fedlex 5 seeds (0--4); Bills--Tweets 5 seeds (0--4); SCOTUS 5 seeds (0--4); CAP 5 seeds (0--4); SCOTUS MiniLM 5 seeds (0--4). SCOTUS with E5-small uses the coverage experiment, and SemEval and CAP their primary runs, each extended from seeds 0--2 by seeds 3--4. Fedlex is a seeded sample of 2{,}784 German/French/Italian article triples of Swiss domestic federal law (SwiLTra's size), with outer splits by whole law. MiniLM results are shown only for three-source SCOTUS, not for the other corpora. AUCs are unflipped. $k$-means LEACE uses the training-silhouette $K$; only Metadata-LEACE uses nuisance labels. Bills--Tweets has no semantic-utility measure (---). Equal rounded values are not evidence of equivalence.
